title: Linear models: the start and the step

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A tank holds four liters of water. A tap adds three liters every minute.

do.text: A tank holds $\cg{4}$ liters. A tap adds $\cw{3}$ liters every minute.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: How much water after any number of minutes?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: After one minute: four, plus three, is seven. After two minutes: four, plus three, plus three, is ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: After three minutes: the same four, plus three threes. Thirteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So after t minutes, it is four, plus three times t.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That is a linear model: where it starts, plus the same step every time.

do.text: Where it starts, plus the same step every time.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each top is three higher than the last: a rise of three for every run of one. So the tops fall on one straight line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: In general: y equals m x plus b.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: m is the step: three more liters for each minute. That is the rate, or slope.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: b is the start: four liters at minute zero. That is the initial value, or the y-intercept, where the line meets the y-axis.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep the steps, and watch what each number does.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start the tank empty. The line slides down to zero, and the step is still three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start with seven liters, and it slides up. Only b changes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to four. Now slow the tap to one liter a minute. The line tilts about its start, and only m changes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Pull the plug, and the tank loses one liter a minute. The step is negative one, so the line falls.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here is a new line. What is its rule?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: It starts at six, and each step goes up two. So V equals two t plus six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now read a model. A candle's height, in centimeters, is H equals sixteen minus two h.

do.text: A candle is $H$ centimeters tall, $h$ hours after it is lit: $H=\cg{16}-\cw{2}h$ What do the $\cg{16}$ and the $\cw{2}$ mean?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: h is the hours since it was lit. What do the sixteen and the two mean?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: At zero hours, nothing has burned. Two times zero is zero, so H is sixteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Sixteen is how tall the candle is when it is lit.

do.text: $\cg{16}$ centimeters: the height when it is lit.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And the two? One hour, two hours, three, four: each hour takes away two centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The flames trace the line: down two for every hour.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Sixteen is an amount. Two is a rate. The start is the number standing alone, even when it is written first.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Sometimes the start is hidden. A line has slope negative two and passes through the point three, one. Write its equation.

do.text: A line has slope $-2$ and passes through the point $(3,1)$. Write its equation in the form $y=mx+b$

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slope negative two: each step to the right goes down two. So each step back, to the left, goes up two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Walk back until x is zero. From one, up to three. Five. Seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So the line starts at seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The equation does the same walk. In y equals m x plus b, put in the slope and the point.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Negative two times three is negative six. Add six to both sides, and b is seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So y equals negative two x, plus seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The one in three, one, is the height at three. It is the start only when x is zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Your turn. A worker buys a uniform, then earns the same amount each hour.

do.text: A worker buys a uniform, then earns the same amount each hour. Find the hourly wage and the uniform's cost.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Net pay is the pay earned, minus the cost of the uniform. After two hours it is negative eight dollars. After four hours, sixteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: From two hours to four, net pay rises from negative eight to sixteen. That is twenty-four dollars in two hours.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Two steps, so each step is twelve. The wage is twelve dollars an hour.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Now walk back. One hour: negative twenty. Zero hours: negative thirty-two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Before any work, the pay is thirty-two dollars below zero. That is the uniform.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So net pay is twelve h, minus thirty-two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The start is negative here, and it still means the amount at zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And a model predicts. After ten hours: twelve times ten, minus thirty-two, is eighty-eight dollars.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One picture holds every linear model: y equals m x plus b.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: b is where it starts, at input zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: m is the step, for each one of input.

do.text: $\cw{m}$: the step, for each 1 of input.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: When the start is hidden, walk back to zero.

do.text: Start hidden? Walk back to zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Where it starts, plus the same step every time.

do.text: Where it starts, plus the same step every time.
